newsitem.title: USA: Paccar treasurer sees production steady.
newsitem.headline: Paccar treasurer sees production steady.

text.p: Paccar Inc treasurer Ron Ranheim said the truck manufacturer saw a slight increase in order rates in the fourth quarter that appears to have carried over into the new year.
Ranheim also said in a conference call after the company's earnings announcement that production rates are expected to remain steady in the near term, although well below peak levels of late 1995.
He said company executives still expect overall truck sales to fall 10 percent in North America and five to 10 percent in Europe this year.
"Compared to the end of the third quarter, it's looking better than we would have thought at that time," he said.
Production recently was boosted to 80 trucks a day from 75 for the company's Kenworth brand, while daily production for Peterbilt trucks has remained at 75 units, he said.

He expected the company's European DAF subsidiary to continue producing at the current level of 66 units a day for the near term, although he said that could come down later in the year given the expected weakness in the European market.
The company had been building 90 Peterbilt trucks and up to 120 Kenworth units daily as recently as late 1995, while DAF daily production peaked at 90 units, Ranheim said.
Ranheim also said Paccar expects to see continued improvement in its Mexican operations, "but of course we're coming off extremely low levels of production."
